authoringProvenance.author: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Pro — unreviewed candidate generation

items.prompt: A window must contain at most K distinct values. The incoming value x currently has frequency 0 in the window. Which state update is correct?
constraints: A frequency map and an integer distinctCount are maintained.
K is a nonnegative integer.
The window is repaired only when distinctCount > K.

options.text: Increment freq[x] and increment distinctCount because x crosses from absent to present; then shrink while distinctCount > K.
Increment distinctCount for every occurrence of x.
Shrink before adding x so the new value is never part of an invalid state.
Clear the map and start a new window whenever x is new.

feedback.reason: Distinct count changes only when a frequency crosses zero; the incoming value must enter state before its violation can be diagnosed.

blocks.text: The map records multiplicity and distinctCount summarizes how many keys have positive frequency. Because freq[x] is zero, adding x creates one new distinct value. If that raises distinctCount above K, left removals repair the window until the count returns to K. Repeated copies of an existing x do not change distinctCount. Shrinking before expansion evaluates the old state and can miss the violation introduced by x; clearing the map discards valid overlap. A transient K+1th key is acceptable only long enough to diagnose and repair the post-expansion violation; it is never an answer-eligible state.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.distinct_every_occurrence: Distinctness counts keys, not elements. A repeated x increases its frequency but not the number of distinct values.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_before_add: The need to shrink is caused by the post-expansion state; checking the old window cannot see the new violation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.replace_map: A new key may require removing only a small prefix. Resetting loses longer valid suffixes and later candidates.

items.prompt: For the longest substring with no repeated character, adding the rightmost character makes its frequency equal to 2. What is the correct frequency-window repair?
constraints: The maintained window must have every character frequency at most 1.
The objective is maximum length.

options.text: Discard the newly added character and keep the previous window unchanged.
Remove characters from the left, updating their frequencies, until the incoming character's frequency returns to 1.
Remove exactly one left character, regardless of which character it is.
Clear the whole frequency map whenever any duplicate appears.

feedback.reason: The violation persists until one copy of the duplicated character leaves; unrelated left removals may be needed first.

blocks.text: A duplicate of the incoming character may have its earlier copy several positions inside the window. Removing one arbitrary left character does not necessarily remove that copy, so repair continues while its frequency is greater than one. Every removal updates the corresponding character count, preserving correct state for later candidates. Dropping the incoming character prevents exploration of windows ending at the current right boundary, while a full reset discards a valid suffix after the earlier duplicate.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.remove_incoming: The optimal no-repeat window may end at the new character after the earlier duplicate is removed.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_once: The first outgoing character can be unrelated to the duplicate, leaving its frequency at 2 and the window invalid.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.clear_all: Only the prefix through the earlier conflicting occurrence must leave; the remaining suffix can still be part of a longer answer.

items.prompt: Order the operations for removing the current leftmost value y from an at-most-K-distinct frequency window.
constraints: distinctCount equals the number of keys with positive frequency.
The current left boundary still points to y.

elements.text: If freq[y] becomes 0, remove y from the map and decrement distinctCount.

feedback.reason: Multiplicity must be updated first; distinctCount changes only if the outgoing key has no remaining copies, then the boundary advances.

blocks.text: The map and boundaries must describe the same range after each completed removal. The outgoing value is read while `left` still identifies it; the frequency transition then determines whether the distinct summary changes.

items: Decrement `freq[y]` to remove this one occurrence from the maintained multiset.
If the new count is zero, delete key `y` and decrement `distinctCount`; if it remains positive, change neither.
Advance `left` only after the state no longer includes the outgoing position.

blocks.title: Presence changes only at 1→0
blocks.text: Decrementing `distinctCount` for every removal undercounts windows containing another copy. Advancing before reading or caching `y` risks updating the new leftmost key instead. The same zero-crossing rule applies to fixed-size frequency windows.

items.prompt: You must count all contiguous ranges containing exactly K distinct values. Why is one standard at-most-K window not sufficient, and what transfer is valid?
constraints: The answer is a count of all qualifying ranges.
K is at least 1.

options.text: After repairing to at most K, add the current window length and treat every counted suffix as exactly K.
Use a fixed window of length K because exactly K distinct values are required.
One at-most window counts ranges with 0..K distinct values; compute atMost(K) − atMost(K−1) to isolate exactly K.
Use one set and count a range whenever its size is K, without tracking multiplicity.

feedback.reason: An at-most window deliberately includes suffixes with fewer than K distinct values; subtracting atMost(K−1) removes them.

blocks.text: After an at-most-K window is repaired for a right boundary, every start from left through right forms a valid suffix, but those suffixes can contain any number of distinct values up to K. Therefore adding right−left+1 computes atMost(K), not exactly K. Running the same counting contract for K−1 and subtracting isolates ranges present in the first count but absent in the second. Exactly K is a property of categories, not length, and frequencies are still needed to move the boundaries correctly.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_window_equals_exact: The counted suffixes include ranges with fewer than K distinct values, so the total overcounts exactly-K ranges.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.fixed_k_length: A range can contain exactly K distinct values while having length greater than K because values may repeat.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.set_without_counts: Without multiplicities, removing one outgoing occurrence can incorrectly erase a value that remains inside the range.

items.prompt: The current window is 'abac'. When the leftmost 'a' leaves, another 'a' remains. What bug occurs if state is only a set and the algorithm removes 'a' from the set unconditionally?
constraints: The set is intended to represent characters currently present.
Duplicate characters may occur.

options.text: There is no bug because a set needs only one copy of each character.
The only effect is an off-by-one error in the window length.
The bug is that set iteration order differs from string order.
The state claims 'a' is absent even though one copy remains, so later distinctness and duplicate checks are wrong.

feedback.reason: A set records presence but cannot decide whether presence survives removal of one among multiple copies.

blocks.text: Before removal, freq['a']=2. After the first 'a' leaves, the correct count is 1, so 'a' remains present. An unconditional set deletion collapses those two states and may admit another 'a' without detecting a duplicate or undercount distinct types. Frequency state resolves the ambiguity by removing the key only on a 1→0 transition. A set becomes sufficient only when the window invariant already guarantees every key occurs at most once and removal is coordinated with a last-position rule.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_bug: The set cannot infer whether another copy remains, which is exactly the information needed after an outgoing duplicate.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.window_too_long_only: The boundary length can be correct while the semantic state is wrong; future validity decisions then fail.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort_order_bug: Iteration order is irrelevant. The defect is lost multiplicity, not presentation order.

items.prompt: A task asks for the longest non-empty contiguous range containing at most K distinct values. What must the algorithm return when K = 0?
constraints: The answer must be a non-empty range.
Every input value belongs to some value category.
K = 0 is allowed by the input contract.

options.text: Return length 0: no non-empty range can contain at most zero distinct values.
Return length 1 because a singleton contains only one distinct value.
Return the full input because the distinct limit disables shrinking.
Reject K as invalid because a frequency window requires K to be positive.

feedback.reason: Every non-empty range contains at least one distinct value, so the at-most-zero contract has no legal non-empty candidate.

blocks.text: The empty range has zero distinct values, but the output contract explicitly requires a non-empty range. As soon as any value enters the window, distinctCount becomes 1 and the repair removes that value again, leaving no non-empty valid state. A singleton therefore violates the limit, and K=0 is valid input rather than an error under the stated contract. The implementation should expose the no-candidate result instead of silently changing the objective to allow an empty answer.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_any_value: A singleton has one distinct value, which exceeds K=0.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.whole_input: The whole input is non-empty and therefore contains at least one distinct value; the limit does not disable repair.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reject_k: The stated contract permits K=0, so rejecting it changes the input domain rather than solving the boundary case.

items.prompt: A window must contain no value more than M times. Adding the rightmost value x makes freq[x] = M + 1. Which repair preserves the longest valid window?
constraints: The frequency cap applies separately to every value.
The objective is maximum window length.
M is a positive integer.

options.text: Remove from the left while freq[x] > M, decrementing each outgoing value's count.
Delete every x from the window immediately, regardless of the values before the earlier x.
Remove exactly one leftmost value because one new value caused the violation.
Clear the map and restart after every value whose count exceeds M.

feedback.reason: The window becomes valid when enough leftmost occurrences leave for the incoming value's count to return to M or below.

blocks.text: The constraint is per value, not a distinct-value count. The earlier copies of x may be separated by other values, so one arbitrary removal may leave freq[x] above M. Moving left while the violated count exceeds M removes only the necessary prefix and preserves the longest valid suffix ending at the current right boundary. Every outgoing value must update the map because it may be a different category whose count matters to later repairs.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.remove_only_x: The window boundary removes a prefix in encounter order; it cannot delete an interior x without also discarding preceding values.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_once_any: The outgoing value may not be the earlier x, so the violation can remain after one removal.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.clear_frequency_state: A full reset discards a valid suffix and is not justified by a local frequency violation.

items.prompt: A window must contain at least one occurrence of every required type in a set R. The leftmost outgoing value is y, and y is required. Order the state updates when y leaves.
constraints: coveredCount records how many required types currently have positive frequency.
The left boundary still points to y before the removal begins.
The window is allowed to remain temporarily incomplete while the right boundary later expands.

elements.text: If y is required and freq[y] becomes 0, decrement coveredCount.
Advance left beyond the outgoing position.

feedback.reason: Coverage changes only when the outgoing required type loses its last occurrence, and the boundary must then advance to match the updated state.

blocks.text: The frequency map distinguishes one remaining copy from complete absence. Decrementing coveredCount for every outgoing required value would mark the window incomplete while another copy is still inside it. Read y while left still identifies the outgoing position, update its multiplicity, apply the zero-crossing rule, and only then advance the boundary.

blocks.title: Coverage is a zero-crossing summary
blocks.text: The required type stops being covered on a 1→0 transition, not on every removal.

items.prompt: For the longest substring with no repeated character, the incoming character x was last seen at index p inside the current window. Which left-boundary update is safe?
constraints: lastSeen[x] stores the most recent index of x.
left is the first index of the current candidate window.
The current window must contain no repeated character.

options.text: Set left = max(left, p + 1), then record lastSeen[x] as the incoming index.
Set left = p so the previous copy remains outside the next comparison.
Increment left once because one duplicate occurrence caused the violation.
Reset left to zero because a repeated character invalidates the whole prefix.

feedback.reason: The previous copy must be excluded, but left must never move backward when the stored occurrence is already outside the current window.

blocks.text: If p is inside the current window, the next valid start is p+1. If p is before left, the current window has no duplicate caused by that stored occurrence, so moving left backward would reintroduce invalid characters and lose a longer suffix. The max operation preserves monotone boundary movement. Recording the incoming position after choosing the new boundary keeps lastSeen synchronized.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.jump_to_p: The previous copy remains at index p inside the candidate, so the resulting window is still invalid.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always_increment_one: The earlier copy may be far from the left boundary; one removal does not necessarily exclude it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reset_zero: Only the prefix through the prior occurrence is known to be unusable; resetting discards valid suffixes.

items.prompt: A longest-window algorithm uses a frequency map, expected O(1) map operations, and left and right boundaries that each move only forward. What are the expected time and auxiliary-space complexities for n input values and a window limit K?
constraints: The map stores only values currently present in the window.
At most K+1 keys exist during a transient at-most-K violation.
Each value is added once and removed at most once.

feedback.reason: Each boundary crosses the input at most once, while the frequency map stores only the active keys permitted by the constraint.

blocks.text: The right boundary performs n additions. Across all repairs, left performs at most n removals, so expected O(1) map work per event gives O(n) total time. The active map has at most K+1 keys during the transient violation described by the contract, hence O(K) auxiliary space. If the input alphabet were fixed, O(K) could simplify to O(1), but K remains explicit here.

items.prompt: When the left pointer removes the last occurrence of a symbol from a frequency-constrained window, what state update is required?
constraints: The constraint counts distinct symbols.
The window may become valid after the removal.

options.text: Decrement the symbol count and remove its key or decrement distinctCount when the count reaches zero.
options.explanation: Distinctness tracks keys with positive frequency.

options.text: Decrement the count but leave distinctCount unchanged forever.
options.explanation: The number of present symbols then becomes stale.

options.text: Delete the key whenever any occurrence leaves, even if another remains.
options.explanation: The symbol is still present while its count is positive.

options.text: Increase distinctCount because a pointer moved left.
options.explanation: Removing the last occurrence decreases the number of distinct symbols.

feedback.reason: Frequency and distinct-count state must stay synchronized at the zero boundary.

blocks.text: A key contributes one distinct symbol while its count is positive. Only the transition from one to zero removes that contribution; removing an earlier duplicate does not.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.decrement_only: The number of present symbols then becomes stale.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.delete_on_first: The symbol is still present while its count is positive.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.increment_distinct: Removing the last occurrence decreases the number of distinct symbols.

items.prompt: For a longest substring with no repeated symbols, why can last-seen indices jump the left pointer?
constraints: The left pointer never moves backward.
Each symbol's last occurrence is stored.

options.text: Set left to max(left, lastSeen[ch]+1) when ch repeats, skipping positions that would include the previous occurrence.
options.explanation: The max prevents a stale occurrence from moving left backward.

options.text: Reset left to zero whenever a duplicate appears so every prefix is reconsidered.
options.explanation: Resetting causes rescans and loses the current valid suffix.

options.text: Move left by one for every duplicate, regardless of the previous index.
options.explanation: A distant previous occurrence may require a larger jump.

options.text: Delete the repeated character from the right end instead of moving left.
options.explanation: The right pointer represents the new input and should not be discarded.

feedback.reason: Last-seen state lets the algorithm jump directly beyond the offending previous occurrence.

blocks.text: The max with the current left boundary is essential: an older occurrence before the current window is irrelevant. Each left and right index still advances monotonically, giving linear time.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reset_zero: Resetting causes rescans and loses the current valid suffix.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.increment_one: A distant previous occurrence may require a larger jump.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.delete_right: The right pointer represents the new input and should not be discarded.

items.prompt: A window constraint allows each symbol at most c occurrences. What event makes the window invalid?
constraints: Counts are maintained for the current contiguous window.
c is a nonnegative integer.

options.text: The window is invalid exactly when some symbol's count becomes greater than c after the right-side addition.
options.explanation: The local cap is violated at that count transition.

options.text: The window becomes invalid as soon as any count equals c.
options.explanation: A cap of c permits exactly c occurrences.

options.text: Only the number of distinct symbols matters, not each symbol's frequency.
options.explanation: A per-symbol cap is different from a distinct-count cap.

options.text: Any nonempty window is invalid because its endpoints differ.
options.explanation: Endpoint distance is unrelated to the occurrence cap.

feedback.reason: Per-symbol caps require inspecting the count of the symbol just added and shrinking until every count is within its own bound.

blocks.text: A distinct-count rule tracks keys; a cap rule tracks each value's multiplicity. The violation is strict excess over c, and removing from the left repairs it monotonically.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.count_equals_c: A cap of c permits exactly c occurrences.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.distinct_exceeds_c: A per-symbol cap is different from a distinct-count cap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.left_equals_right: Endpoint distance is unrelated to the occurrence cap.

items.prompt: What complexity assumption is needed when claiming a frequency-map sliding window is O(n)?
constraints: The input has n positions.
The implementation uses a map keyed by symbols.

options.text: Each map update and lookup is expected O(1) or otherwise bounded by the symbol domain, and each pointer advances at most n times.
options.explanation: Both state-operation cost and pointer amortization support the claim.

options.text: Map operations are free because they are not part of pointer movement.
The map must be sorted after every update to guarantee linear time.
The inner shrink loop makes the algorithm O(n^2) automatically.
options.explanation: Monotone left movement makes total shrink operations O(n).

feedback.reason: The linear claim combines amortized pointer movement with the cost model for map operations.

blocks.text: Right and left each advance at most n times. If map operations are expected constant time, total state work is linear; a different map model or costly key comparison must be included in the analysis.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.quadratic_shrink: Monotone left movement makes total shrink operations O(n).
